ledger.claim: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing length of the trip and states that trip_record.actual_distance_km 'may NOT be cited for the threshold test'. The trace measures 29.98 km across 229 fixes, with a 10-second sample interval, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. The distance the rider was billed against is therefore 29.98 km and the excess over the 24.0 km booked optimal is 5.98 km, not the rounded 6.00 km the receipt line implies.

Both POL-RD-01 gates pass on the trace figures. Excess of 5.98 km is 24.92% of the 24.0 km optimal route, which exceeds the 20% establishment gate, and 5.98 km is far above the 0.8 km absolute gate. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own telemetry, recorded as 'established' by the derived block, and it is not de minimis.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. Trip identifier TRP-00111 is the same on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown; the trace's first fix at 2026-08-03T07:47:40+08:00 is exactly the recorded trip start on the trip record, and the trace's last fix at 08:25:40 is the recorded end. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a general assertion that a road was closed does not discharge it unless an advisory artifact is named to carry it.

The driver cannot fall back on a rider-requested detour. The only rider message on this trip is 'as long as i reach by 8.30'; it names no place and no road, and the driver's own message is a notification ('i come off at bukit panjang ok'), not a request for rider consent. Both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run at all. POL-RD-04 says the clause is then unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

POL-RD-03 exonerates a deviation only where the advisory names a road or segment that the optimal route traverses. The optimal route for this trip was produced by the platform's routing engine from an LTA traffic snapshot taken at 07:44, thirty-four minutes after this closure advisory went live at 07:10, and it still returned 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound' with no diversion. That route estimate is the very baseline POL-RD-01 fixes for this trip, and it is not consistent with the closed segment lying on the corridor the rider was billed against. The advisory cannot be used to wipe out 5.98 km of extra distance without the judge resolving that inconsistency first.

POL-RD-03(c) also requires the actual route to leave the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoin it after. The trace-derived facts supplied for this trip report fix counts, distances and speeds, not corridor geometry: 229 fixes, minimum distance 0.0 m, mean 7038.8 m, maximum 15193.2 m, four distinct speeds up to 71.0 kph. Nothing in that derived data places the vehicle on the diversion or shows where it left and rejoined the corridor, so on the present record that limb rests on the driver's own counterparty statement and his own chat message alone.

If the closure does not excuse the distance, the remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the booked optimal because no POL-RD-03 adjustment applies: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x the 1.0 surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 31.00. The refund is charged_total 37.74 less 31.00 = 6.74, rounded up to SGD 6.75. That is the same order as the rider's own account that this route is 'never more than $32'; it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share.

If the judge cannot resolve the tension between the advisory's intersects_route flag and the 07:44-snapshot optimal route that kept the PIE westbound, POL-RD-10(7) applies: the driver's exoneration and the rider's measurement then rest on admissible yet mutually contradictory matter of comparable strength, and the case must go to a human reviewer. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalation holds the disputed amount rather than leaving it as a standing charge, which is the outcome the rider seeks on a record that cannot settle the question.

ledger.claim: The GPS trace for this trip is clean and unimpaired for policy purposes. It covers 100% of the trip with 229 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval, reports no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of the impairment limbs in POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises on the trace. The threshold test in POL-RD-01 therefore runs on the governing trace figure of 29.98 km, which is marginally BELOW the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy carried on the trip record — the trace, not the trip record, governs.

On the governing trace figure the arithmetic gate in POL-RD-01 is passed, and I do not contest that much: the excess is 5.98 km, which is 24.92% of the 24.0 km booked optimal, over both the 20% and the 0.8 km tests. What matters for the driver is that the same numbers fall far short of the ADDITIONAL materiality tests — 5.98 km is under the 8.0 km figure and 24.92% is under the 50% figure — so this is a deviation, but not a MATERIAL one, POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not triggered, and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available on this trip.

The first limb of POL-RD-03 is satisfied on the face of the artifact: the traffic advisory names the Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after the Clementi Rd exit — the very segment the booked optimal route uses, the optimal route being BKE southbound then PIE westbound per the routing engine source on the trip record — and the fare derived block records that the advisory intersects the route. The rider's assertion that 'I did not see any closure' is contradicted by a third-party LTA_DATAMALL record of a HIGH severity, all-lanes closure.

The second limb of POL-RD-03 is satisfied: the advisory is valid from 07:10 to 09:30 on the trip date and the trace runs from 07:47:40 to 08:25:40, an overlap of 41.5 minutes measured on the artifact itself. The vehicle was on the road network for that entire window, so it would necessarily have reached the affected segment well inside the advisory's validity, with far more than the 15 minute buffer at each end that POL-RD-03 allows.

The third limb of POL-RD-03 is satisfied and is corroborated by three records that agree. The driver left the optimal corridor at Bukit Panjang and ran Upper Bukit Timah and the AYE before rejoining to the booked dropoff at one-north — the same diversion the advisory itself prescribes ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'), and the same shape the rider describes in his own claim. The driver told the rider exactly this at 07:54:20 ('boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok'); the rider read it at 07:54:48 and answered at 07:54:55, and the dropoff was never amended.

The cap in POL-RD-03 does not bite on this trip, so the WHOLE of the excess is exonerated. The justified excess is the lesser of the measured 5.98 km and 1.30 x (29.2 km shortest lawful alternative - 24.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 1.30 x 5.2 + 1.00 = 7.76 km. The lesser figure is 5.98 km — exactly the measured excess — which means nothing is left over to refund. This is the arithmetic the fare derived block itself publishes as cap_km and justified_excess_km.

Running POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route, as POL-RD-03 requires, the charge stands. The adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km with a duration of 37.5 minutes (30.0 minutes scaled by 29.98/24.0, the trip record carrying no amended duration). Recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 37.585. Charged_total = 37.74. Refund = 37.74 - 37.585 = SGD 0.155, which is below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome on the fare is NO_ACTION. I state the three figures on separate lines as the clause requires: charged_total 37.74, recomputed_fare 37.585, refund 0.155.

The only pass-through correction a closure exoneration leaves open is the off-route ERP refund under POL-RD-09(2), and on this trip there is nothing to pass back: the fare breakdown itemises no gantry lines at all — the erp_gantries array is empty and both the on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route ERP totals are 0.00 — so no standalone correction is due and nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, in accordance with the anti-double-count rule in POL-RD-09(1).

The rider's threshold showing under POL-RD-08 does not go unanswered, because the driver does not meet it with a general assertion that traffic was bad: he points to a specific artifact and a specific clause — LTA advisory ADV-20260803-014, which is in the pool, names the closed segment, and overlaps the trip window — and invokes POL-RD-03 on it. That is precisely what POL-RD-08 requires of the driver once the excess is shown, and the rider has filed no artifact contradicting the advisory.

No mandatory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires. The trip identifier TRP-00111 matches across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown; the trace is unimpaired and complete; the timestamps run forwards and consistently from request 07:44:10 through to dropoff 08:25:40; the exculpatory clause is invoked against an artifact that exists, covers the trip window and carries every field POL-RD-03 needs; the residual refund of SGD 0.155 is nowhere near the SGD 150.00 ceiling; and every charge line has a counterpart, with no ERP or surcharge lines at all. This case can and should be ruled on the record.

Even if the rider were to reach for a repeat-deviation argument, POL-RD-06's test is not met and no conduct referral is licensed. The only two fields that clause permits are driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d: the flag count is 0, not the 3 or more the clause requires, and 0 divided by 588 completed trips in 90 days is 0.00, not the 0.05 the clause requires with at least 40 trips. No pattern, no uplift, no referral — and POL-GEN-01 forbids me from reaching for any other field on that artifact, as it forbids the rider.

The consequence the rider seeks does not follow even if the closure is set aside entirely: the deviation is established but not material, and the POL-RD-02 refund on the unadjusted route would be 37.74 - 31.000 = SGD 6.74, rounded up to SGD 6.75 payable — not the SGD 8.00 contested. With the closure exonerated under POL-RD-03 the figure drops to SGD 0.155, below de minimis. Either way the driver did not overcharge, and on a rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION leaves the present charge standing and the driver whole.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both of you.

WHAT HAPPENED, IN FIGURES. The trip was charged 37.74 SGD (fare_breakdown charged_total). It ran 29.98 km on the GPS trace (trace_distance_km), which governs over the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. Against the 24.0 km booked optimal, the excess is 5.98 km, i.e. 24.92%. That passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation IS established. It does not reach the materiality gates (8.0 km / 50%), so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check, uplift or conduct referral arises.

WHY NOTHING IS REFUNDED. The deviation is fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory ADV-20260803-014 records a HIGH-severity all-lanes closure on the PIE towards Tuas after Clementi Rd, 07:10 to 09:30. On the computed facts it intersects the booked optimal corridor (intersects_route = true) and it overlaps the trip window (07:47:40 to 08:25:40). The actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined after it: both accounts agree on the same diversion (off at Bukit Panjang, Upper Bukit Timah, the AYE), the advisory itself prescribes exactly that diversion, and the driver told the rider so in the chat at 07:54:20, inside the trip window, with the rider reading and answering it. The exoneration cap is the lesser of the measured 5.98 km and 1.30 x (29.2 km shortest lawful alternative - 24.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 7.76 km. The lesser figure is 5.98 km, so the whole measured excess is justified.

POL-RD-02 then runs against the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km; 37.5 minutes, the 30.0-minute booked duration scaled by 29.98/24.0). This is set out on separate lines as the clause requires: charged_total 37.74; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 37.585; refund = 37.74 - 37.585 = 0.155 SGD. That is below the 0.50 SGD de minimis, so no refund issues. The fare breakdown carries no gantry lines at all (ERP totals 0.00, on and off optimal route), so the POL-RD-09(2) pass-through correction available on a closure exoneration comes to nothing, and no other pass-through or billing-integrity line exists.

THE RIDER'S POINTS. The threshold showing under POL-RD-08 is accepted: the same trip TRP-00111 appears on the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the excess of 5.98 km measured from an unimpaired trace meets POL-RD-01. A rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is correctly not available: the only rider message is 'as long as i reach by 8.30', which names no place or road, and both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null, so the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The suggestion that the routing engine's 07:44 snapshot, which still returned BKE southbound then PIE westbound, contradicts the advisory is rejected: the booked optimal is the baseline POL-RD-01 fixes, the intersection of the advisory with that corridor is a computed fact this tribunal does not re-derive, and the clause notes expressly forbid reading a substitute optimal out of the free text of optimal_route_source. It does not create a POL-RD-10(7) contradiction, because the rider opposes the advisory with no admissible artifact of comparable strength - 'I did not see any closure' cites no evidence and carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The rider's alternative arithmetic (37.74 - 31.00 = 6.74, rounded 6.75) is the correct figure ONLY if the closure did not apply; because it does apply, that figure is superseded. On the profile points both sides are right: POL-GEN-01 confines the profiles to the tests that name their fields, nothing on either profile is used against anyone, and the driver's lifetime counters are context only.

No mandatory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 229 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps), timestamps run forward and consistently, the exculpatory clause is invoked on an artifact that exists, covers the window and carries every field it needs, the residual refund is nowhere near 150.00 SGD, no charge line is unmatched and no two sides rest on mutually contradictory admissible evidence. Because this is a rider-filed dispute, NO_ACTION leaves the existing charge and payment status as they stand; the disputed 8.00 SGD is not refunded and no compensation is payable to the driver. One open observation for the record, which does not change the outcome: the routing-engine wording on the trip record is not used to build the optimal, and a customer-facing note could explain to riders why a genuinely closed expressway can still lengthen a billed trip while leaving no refund due.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
